title: A copy guard catches recitation, not overlap
statement: Flag an answer as copied only when it recites a long unbroken run of the source, not for shared words, which correct answers about a short text will reuse.
example: A check counting words shared with a two-word definition, 'to forgive', rejected accurate explanations of two taught words.
detail: In a full student sweep of the rebuilt Grade 5 lessons, correct explanations of two taught words were rejected by a deterministic client check that counted words shared with the definition and ignored the explanation around them. With a two-word definition, an accurate explanation was especially likely to fail. The repair limited the check to definition-only recitation and left meaning to the judge; the rejected explanations were then accepted unchanged, and the repaired code passed 19 regression cases, copy-only negatives among them.
against: Narrowing the guard is safe only while a judge still checks meaning: "It does not grant a pass merely for adding words." (`grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/review-readiness/curriculum-alignment/rebuild/integration/full-student-sweep/rehearsal-pardon-scoring-review.md`, line 5). The thresholds, a run of at least 8 tokens and 0.85 total overlap, are design values for answers in an early-grade reading app; no measured false-flag rate is recorded.

evidence.quote: The revised rehearsal answer and the pardon answer were rejected by a deterministic client check that counted shared definition words. It ignored the original explanation around those words. With a two-word definition such as “to forgive,” an accurate explanation was especially likely to fail.
7f32fd95 narrows the Grade 5 copy guard. Definition-only copies still fail; elaboration is judged for meaning. Actual rehearsal/pardon explanations accepted unchanged.
The actual hook passed 19 regressions, including the reported answers, copy-only negatives and an incorrect elaboration rejected by the scorer.
verbatim-copy = a contiguous verbatim run ≥ 8 tokens AND ≥ 0.85 total n-gram overlap, so a correct short-passage answer that reuses topic words is not falsely flagged
**Pre-gate + garbage flag:** too-short, verbatim-copy, and non-attempts (gibberish, repeated filler, "idk") are caught and forced to a re-type before the LLM even scores.
